newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Data shows Australia housing upturn shaky - industry.
newsitem.headline: Data shows Australia housing upturn shaky - industry.

text.p: An Australian building industry group said figures released earlier on Friday showed the housing industry's recovery was still in a tentative phase.

"The February figures clearly demonstrate that there remains considerable uncertainty in the minds of new home buyers," Master Builders Australia national director economics and housing Wilhelm Harnisch said in a statement.
"Last year's cut in interest rates and the competitive home loan packages have failed to sustain a lift in new housing demand."
Australian building approvals fell a seasonally-adjusted 3.7 percent in February to 11,578 from 12,020 in January and 10,407 in February 1996.
"Any suggestion of an interest rate rise would clearly be premature given the February fall in approval figures," Harnisch said.
But Real Estate Institute of Australia Ltd president Don Brindley said the February downturn was consistent with the pace of the recovery.
"The Australian housing sector has entered into its next upswing," Brindley said in a statement.
"However, there is not likely to be the kind of property boom which shook markets in the late 1980s."
Both industry groups blamed Australia's high unemployment rate for the softness in the housing market.
"The government needs to prove its commitment to the rest of Australia by doing something about the unemployment problem currently crippling Australia's potential," Brindley said.
Australia's unemployment rate was at 8.8 percent in February, up from 8.6 percent in the previous month.
